newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $65 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $65 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was slow near midday Monday, with light sales reported at $65.00 per cwt, unchanged from the bulk of last week's activity, according to feedlot sources.
About 3,000 head sold of steers and heifers which will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas, USDA and private sources said.
No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said.
Sales had been expected to be light going into the Christmas holiday on Wednesday, some cattle feeders said.
Most feedlots were pricing cattle at $67.00, with scattered bids reported at $65.00, sources said.

Fed cattle prices were expected to be supported by a firm outlook for beef prices. Beef values were seen underpinned by projected strong retail demand for advertising features the first two weeks of January, sources said.
Wholesale beef on Friday was quoted up $0.18 to $1.08 per cwt on 256 loads of fabricated cuts sold, USDA said.
